answer_1.quote: We tackle the problem of generating high-quality CS text ... we treat this problem as a translation task where the source and target languages are monolingual Hindi text and Hindi-English CS text, respectively.
answer_1.outputs: Hindi-English code‑switched sentences generated from monolingual Hindi inputs

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the quality of sentences generated by TCS using BLEU scores, BERTScore, perplexity of language models, self‑BLEU and diversity (gzip) metrics.

answer_3.quote: We add a fully connected layer over the M‑BERT base architecture that takes the [CLS] token as its input to predict the probability of the sentence being real or fake.
methods: binary classification of real vs. fake CS sentences

answer_4.quote: We sampled 150 sentences each ... three linguistic experts in Hindi ... were asked to provide scores ranging between 1 and 5 ... under three heads: 'Syntactic correctness', 'Semantic correctness' and 'Naturalness'.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated each generated sentence on syntactic correctness, semantic correctness and naturalness on a 1‑5 Likert scale.
